items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: I remember the fellow who owned it was an old Irishman named Ames O'Brien, yeah, and so we played up there with him.

ctx.x: Now, what about Campbell, the drummer, Jimmy Campbell. Was that --

Yes, Jimmy Campbell. He was a fellow out of Brooklyn. He was a drummer, and I don't remember just how I got in contact with him. But it was a summer job, up in Albany, at this roadhouse. You know, they used to call them roadhouses in those days. They were out of town and of course this was during prohibition, and they sold bootleg whiskey and the gangsters. I think it was -- it was a gangster house, of course it was. I remember the fellow who owned it was an old Irishman named Ames O'Brien, yeah, and so we played…
guitar player and myself, four pieces. Yeah. Then later on, we added another piece. We added Johnny Russell. Did you ever hear of Johnny Russell, a tenor player?
